notes_for_editor: Thin record: a list entry, two OpenStreetMap tags and one map-site page. No build date, agency, staffing, fires, history or current status was found in the pages read. The story is about 100 words, under the 120-word floor, because nothing more is sourced; it was not padded. The list gives the elevation as a bare number; the map site reads 463 feet (141 metres), which settles the unit, and the story now cites that map site for the feet and metres. A search snippet from aboutus.com gave 141 ft (463 m), which reverses the units; that page was rate-limited and not read, so it is not used. The map site's coordinates (32.09586, -84.22831) differ from the list's by about 25 m. The gfc-324 and BLL-41120 labels are printed as the list has them; the pages read do not explain them. The name is generic, so check the coordinates on a map before a human relies on the record. The tnlandforms page names no author, so its footnote gives the site name only.
